main_text.p:
culis apparet rubor,& calor percipitur. Reliqua uero fymptomata mitiora funt, & animi affectus mites,& cu rifu fiunt.Si praeterea ob ftomachi uitium quis comitia
liter concidit,tum fluctuationes, intercisionesq;,aut compunctiones uentriculi antecedunt, aut interdum uel naufea, aut cardialgia, aut deniq; lipothymia. Celerius corripit uacuo uentriculo,quā pleno,quoniam abstinentia humores in eo exacuuntur.Quandoq; hominem iugulat ob infultuum crebritatem,qui,ut plurimum in uomitionem alias pituitosam, alias biliosam definunt. Veruntamen qui pituitosus eft humor morbum excitat tempore fatietatis,quae naufeam parit. Propterea uomitu leuatur aeger,ut alui folutione. Biliofo autem nimia inedia paroxyfmu inducit, quae affectus biliofi antecedunt,ut oris amaror, cardiogmus,fitis, calor acris totius corporis.Si deniq; pituita cum melancholico humore coniuncta fit, guftus aegrotantis acidus erit,uana ppetuo cogitabit ille,ac fecu loquetur.Omnia(ut fummatim dica) fymptomata uel maiora erut, uel minora,ut alteruter humor uincet. Propterea fi melancholicus humor dominetur pituitę, tuc

page.notes: The first lines of the page are printed as "culis apparet rubor" with the word beginning "Re-" split across lines; "fatieta-tis" is read as printed. The word "tuc" at the end of the last full line may be an abbreviation of tunc with a tilde; it is transcribed as printed. "nesq;," is read as printed with the q; mark; the broken word "intercisio-" is partly obscured by the line above. The line beginning "lancholicus" appears to be missing its first letter in the scan. Greek and Hebrew: none. Marginal notes: none. The first line of the page continues the previous page, so cont="true" is set. The word "exci-" at the bottom right is the catchword.
